Do you experience any pulsatile tinnitus, visual obscurations (graying out of vision), or a sensation of "whooshing" in your ears when you move? The blood pressure is mildly elevated but within acceptable limits for a hypertensive crisis, and the ESR is normal, which makes giant cell arteritis less likely. Given the bilateral visual acuity loss and retinal hemorrhages, do you experience transient visual obscurations or do you see halos around lights? Also, have you noticed any recent weight loss or excessive fatigue?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (Pseudotumor Cerebri).

The clinical picture of bilateral visual loss, retinal hemorrhages/edema (suggesting papilledema), and headache in a patient without CSF pleocytosis (normal ESR, no infectious signs) strongly supports this diagnosis. The normal blood pressure and lack of systemic symptoms further rule out hypertensive emergency or giant cell arteritis.
